definition: Compassion is the capacity to understand another person’s emotional suffering and respond in a way that supports trust and cooperation. In this packet, it is described as an important part of nursing that benefits both patients and nurses.

reasons: The definition generalizes compassion beyond the packet: the source discusses compassion specifically in nursing, not as a general psychological capacity.

“Understand another person’s emotional suffering” is not directly supported; the packet says nurses understand patients’ emotions and patients’ suffering is mentioned only in the context of compassion fatigue.

“Respond in a way that supports trust and cooperation” is only partly supported: the packet says compassion can help build trust and patients may cooperate more, but it does not define compassion as that kind of response.

The packet supports that compassion helps nurses understand patients’ emotions and build trust, but it does not explicitly define compassion as a general "capacity to...respond" to "emotional suffering" (those phrases are more specific than the packet’s wording).

The packet links compassion to reduced conflict, patients cooperating more, and improved patient/nurse outcomes, but “respond in a way that supports trust and cooperation” is not stated as part of a direct definition of compassion.
